source.text: לֹ֥א תִשָּׂ֖א שֵׁ֣מַע שָׁ֑וְא אַל־תָּ֤שֶׁת יָֽדְךָ֙ עִם־רָשָׁ֔ע לִהְיֹ֖ת עֵ֥ד חָמָֽס׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Not you must lift up a report of falsehood. Do not put your hand with a wicked [one] to be a witness of violence.

en.L: You shall not take up a false report. Do not put your hand with a wicked [one] to be a witness of violence.
en.B: Do not pass along a false report. Do not join forces with a wicked person by serving as a witness whose words do violence.
en.R: Do not spread untrue stories about others. Do not help a guilty person by telling lies in court that will hurt someone.

es.L: No levantarás un rumor falso. No pongas tu mano con un malvado para ser testigo de violencia.
es.B: No propagarás rumores falsos. No te aliarás con el malvado prestándote a ser un testigo cuyas palabras causen violencia.
es.R: No andes contando historias falsas sobre otros. No ayudes a un culpable diciendo mentiras en un juicio que le hagan daño a alguien.

fr.L: Tu ne lèveras pas de rumeur mensongère. Ne mets pas ta main avec un méchant pour être témoin de violence.
fr.B: Tu ne colporteras pas de faux bruits. Tu ne t’associeras pas au méchant en devenant un témoin dont les paroles font violence.
fr.R: Ne répands pas d’histoires fausses sur les autres. N’aide pas un coupable en mentant au tribunal pour faire du tort à quelqu’un.

sw.L: Usiinue habari ya uongo. Usiweke mkono wako pamoja na mwovu ili kuwa shahidi wa dhuluma.
sw.B: Usieneze habari za uongo. Usishirikiane na mtu mwovu kwa kuwa shahidi ambaye maneno yake yanaleta dhuluma.
sw.R: Usieneze hadithi za uongo kuhusu wengine. Usimsaidie mtu mwenye hatia kwa kusema uongo mahakamani na kumdhuru mtu.

decisions.choice: take up a false report: start or spread a groundless rumor
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift or carry. A false report may be lifted up by being started or carried on by being repeated, and both are forbidden. It is the same word for "false" as in the commandment about the name (20:7).

decisions.choice: put your hand with ... a witness of violence: side with the guilty by testimony that does harm
decisions.reason: To put one's hand with someone is to join him in a cause. A "witness of violence" is one whose testimony is meant to wrong another, even to take a life (Deuteronomy 19:16-19; Psalm 35:11). The ninth commandment is applied to the court (20:16).

decisions.choice: telling lies in court
decisions.reason: Readable spells out that the witness gives false testimony in a court case, as the context of verses 1-3 and 6-8 shows.

source.text: לֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרֵֽי־רַבִּ֖ים לְרָעֹ֑ת וְלֹא־תַעֲנֶ֣ה עַל־רִ֗ב לִנְטֹ֛ת אַחֲרֵ֥י רַבִּ֖ים לְהַטֹּֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: Not you must be after many [people] to evil deeds, and not you must answer on a case at law to turn aside after many [people] to thrust aside.

en.L: You shall not be after many to do evil; and you shall not answer in a lawsuit, turning aside after many, to pervert [justice].
en.B: Do not follow a crowd to do evil. And when you speak in a lawsuit, do not lean toward the many so as to bend justice.
en.R: Do not do wrong just because many others are doing it. When you speak as a witness in court, do not go along with the crowd and make the outcome unfair.

es.L: No irás tras muchos para [hacer] el mal, ni responderás en un pleito desviándote tras muchos para torcer [la justicia].
es.B: No seguirás a la multitud para hacer el mal. Y cuando declares en un pleito, no te inclinarás hacia la mayoría para torcer la justicia.
es.R: No hagas lo malo solo porque muchos lo hacen. Cuando hables como testigo en un juicio, no te dejes llevar por la mayoría para que el resultado sea injusto.

fr.L: Tu ne seras pas à la suite de la multitude pour [faire] le mal, et tu ne répondras pas dans un procès en penchant à la suite de la multitude pour faire dévier [la justice].
fr.B: Tu ne suivras pas la foule pour faire le mal. Et quand tu témoigneras dans un procès, tu ne pencheras pas du côté du grand nombre pour faire fléchir la justice.
fr.R: Ne fais pas le mal simplement parce que beaucoup d’autres le font. Quand tu es témoin au tribunal, ne suis pas la foule pour fausser le résultat du procès.

sw.L: Usiwe nyuma ya wengi kwa [kutenda] maovu; wala usijibu katika shauri ukigeuka nyuma ya wengi ili kupotosha [haki].
sw.B: Usiufuate umati kutenda maovu. Na unapotoa ushahidi katika shauri, usiegemee upande wa wengi ili kupotosha haki.
sw.R: Usifanye mabaya kwa sababu tu wengi wanayafanya. Unaposhuhudia mahakamani, usifuate umati na kufanya matokeo ya shauri yasiwe ya haki.

decisions.choice: many: the majority, the crowd
decisions.reason: The word means "many". It may also mean "great ones", the powerful (Job 32:9), but the contrast with the poor in verse 3 suggests a crowd or majority, whose weight can push a witness or a judge.

decisions.choice: answer in a lawsuit ... to pervert: give testimony that bends the verdict
decisions.reason: To "answer" in a case is to testify (20:16). The last verb, to thrust aside, has no object; the sense is to turn justice away from what is right, as in verse 6.

decisions.choice: bend justice / make the outcome unfair
decisions.reason: The Hebrew leaves the object of "thrust aside" unstated; Balanced and Readable supply it. Literal brackets "justice".

source.text: וְדָ֕ל לֹ֥א תֶהְדַּ֖ר בְּרִיבֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And a poor [person] not you must honor in his case at law.

en.L: And a poor [one] you shall not favor in his lawsuit.
en.B: Do not give special treatment to {{gender:a poor person|a poor man}} in {{gender:their|his}} lawsuit either.
en.R: In court, do not take a poor person's side out of pity.

es.L: Y al pobre no lo favorecerás en su pleito.
es.B: Tampoco darás trato de favor a {{gender:una persona pobre|un hombre pobre}} en su pleito.
es.R: En un juicio, no te pongas de parte del pobre solo por lástima.

fr.L: Et le pauvre, tu ne le favoriseras pas dans son procès.
fr.B: Tu ne favoriseras pas non plus {{gender:une personne pauvre|un homme pauvre}} dans son procès.
fr.R: Au tribunal, ne prends pas le parti d’un pauvre par pitié.

sw.L: Wala maskini usimpendelee katika shauri lake.
sw.B: Wala usimpendelee mtu maskini katika shauri lake.
sw.R: Mahakamani, usimpendelee maskini kwa sababu tu unamhurumia.

decisions.choice: do not favor a poor man: justice must not lean even toward the weak
decisions.reason: The verb means to honor or show regard. A judge or witness must not tilt a case toward a poor man because he is poor, just as he must not tilt it toward the crowd (verse 2). Leviticus 19:15 forbids both: favoring the poor and deferring to the great.

decisions.choice: poor: the reading of the Hebrew text
alternatives: do not favor a great man in his lawsuit
decisions.reason: The Hebrew manuscripts read "poor". A change of one letter would give "great", and Leviticus 19:15 names the poor and the great side by side, so some have proposed reading "a great man" here. That reading is a conjecture, not one found in a Hebrew manuscript; and verse 6 shows the law guarding the poor from both sides.

decisions.choice: out of pity
decisions.reason: Readable names the reason such favor would be shown, to make the point of the law clear.

source.text: כִּ֣י תִפְגַּ֞ע שׁ֧וֹר אֹֽיִבְךָ֛ א֥וֹ חֲמֹר֖וֹ תֹּעֶ֑ה הָשֵׁ֥ב תְּשִׁיבֶ֖נּוּ לֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: If you meet the ox of your enemy or his donkey wandering off, certainly you will return it to him.

en.L: If you meet your enemy's ox or his donkey wandering off, you shall surely return it to him.
en.B: When you find your enemy's ox or donkey gone astray, you must lead it back to its owner.
en.R: Suppose you find your enemy's ox or donkey wandering loose. You must take it back to its owner.

es.L: Si encuentras el buey de tu enemigo o su asno descarriado, ciertamente se lo devolverás.
es.B: Cuando encuentres extraviado el buey o el asno de tu enemigo, se lo llevarás de vuelta a su dueño.
es.R: Si encuentras suelto el buey o el burro de tu enemigo, tienes que devolvérselo a su dueño.

fr.L: Si tu rencontres le bœuf de ton ennemi ou son âne égaré, tu le lui ramèneras sans faute.
fr.B: Si tu trouves le bœuf ou l’âne de ton ennemi qui s’est égaré, tu le ramèneras à son propriétaire.
fr.R: Imagine que tu trouves le bœuf ou l’âne de ton ennemi qui erre tout seul. Tu dois le rendre à son propriétaire.

sw.L: Ukikutana na ng'ombe wa adui yako au punda wake akipotea, hakika utamrudishia.
sw.B: Ukimkuta ng'ombe au punda wa adui yako amepotea, utamrudisha kwa mwenyewe.
sw.R: Ukimwona ng'ombe au punda wa adui yako anazurura ovyo, lazima umrudishe kwa mwenyewe.

decisions.choice: your enemy's ox: help is owed even to an enemy
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 22:1-4 gives the same law for a "brother". Here it reaches to one's enemy, perhaps an opponent at law, set as it is among laws about the courts. Being in a dispute with someone does not excuse leaving his animal to be lost (compare Proverbs 25:21).

decisions.choice: its owner
decisions.reason: "To him" means the enemy who owns the animal; Balanced and Readable say "its owner".

source.text: כִּֽי־תִרְאֶ֞ה חֲמ֣וֹר שֹׂנַאֲךָ֗ רֹבֵץ֙ תַּ֣חַת מַשָּׂא֔וֹ וְחָדַלְתָּ֖ מֵעֲזֹ֣ב ל֑וֹ עָזֹ֥ב תַּעֲזֹ֖ב עִמּֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: If you see the donkey of [one who] hates you lying down under its load, and you will refrain from leaving it to him, certainly you will rearrange [it] with him.

en.L: If you see the donkey of one who hates you lying under its load, and you would hold back from leaving [it] to {{gender:them|him}}, you shall surely help with {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: Suppose the donkey of someone who hates you has sunk down under its burden. However much you may wish to leave it to {{gender:them|him}}, you must work with {{gender:them|him}} to set it free.
en.R: You may see the donkey of someone who hates you lying on the ground under a heavy load. You might not want to help, but you must help that person get the donkey up again.

es.L: Si ves el asno de quien te odia echado bajo su carga, y te retraerías de dejárselo, ciertamente ayudarás {{gender:junto a esa persona|junto a él}}.
es.B: Si el asno de alguien que te odia se ha desplomado bajo su carga, por mucho que quieras dejárselo {{gender:a esa persona|a él}}, tendrás que trabajar {{gender:con esa persona|con él}} para liberarlo.
es.R: Puede que veas tirado en el suelo, bajo una carga pesada, el burro de alguien que te odia. Tal vez no quieras ayudar, pero tienes que ayudar a esa persona a levantar al burro.

fr.L: Si tu vois l’âne de {{gender:la personne qui te hait|celui qui te hait}} couché sous sa charge, et que tu te retiennes de [le] lui abandonner, tu [le] dégageras sans faute avec {{gender:elle|lui}}.
fr.B: Si l’âne de quelqu’un qui te hait s’est affaissé sous son fardeau, tu auras beau vouloir le laisser à son propriétaire, tu devras travailler avec {{gender:cette personne|lui}} pour le dégager.
fr.R: Tu verras peut-être l’âne de quelqu’un qui te déteste couché par terre sous une lourde charge. Tu n’auras peut-être pas envie d’aider, mais tu dois aider cette personne à remettre l’âne debout.

sw.L: Ukimwona punda wa yule anayekuchukia amelala chini ya mzigo wake, nawe ungejizuia kumwachia, hakika utamsaidia pamoja naye.
sw.B: Huenda punda wa mtu anayekuchukia ameanguka chini ya mzigo wake. Hata kama ungependa kumwachia mwenyewe, utashirikiana naye kumfungua.
sw.R: Huenda ukamwona punda wa mtu anayekuchukia amelala chini akiwa na mzigo mzito. Huenda hutaki kusaidia, lakini lazima umsaidie mtu huyo kumwinua punda tena.

decisions.choice: leaving ... help: the same verb used two ways
alternatives: you shall surely leave it with him (unload it together)
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to leave or abandon, and the first time it has that sense: you may want to leave the animal to its owner. The second time it must mean the opposite, to help or set free, perhaps a second verb of the same sound meaning to arrange or put right (compare Nehemiah 3:8). The play on words sets what one would like to do against what one must do. Deuteronomy 22:4 gives the same law with the plain verb "lift up".

decisions.choice: and you would hold back: a concession
decisions.reason: The clause is best taken as a concession: even if you would rather refrain from helping, you must help. Some take it as a command ("refrain from leaving it"), with the same result.

decisions.choice: get the donkey up again
decisions.reason: Readable says what the help is: getting the fallen animal back on its feet.

source.text: לֹ֥א תַטֶּ֛ה מִשְׁפַּ֥ט אֶבְיֹנְךָ֖ בְּרִיבֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Not you must turn aside the justice of your needy [person] in his case at law.

en.L: You shall not turn aside the justice of your needy [one] in his lawsuit.
en.B: Do not pervert the justice due to your poor when they bring a case.
en.R: When poor people among you go to court, do not twist the law against them.

es.L: No torcerás el derecho de tu necesitado en su pleito.
es.B: No pervertirás la justicia que se debe a tus pobres cuando presenten un pleito.
es.R: Cuando los pobres de tu pueblo vayan a juicio, no tuerzas la ley en su contra.

fr.L: Tu ne feras pas dévier le droit de ton indigent dans son procès.
fr.B: Tu ne fausseras pas le droit dû à tes pauvres lorsqu’ils ont un procès.
fr.R: Quand des pauvres de chez toi vont au tribunal, ne tords pas la loi contre eux.

sw.L: Usipotoshe haki ya mhitaji wako katika shauri lake.
sw.B: Usiipotoshe haki wanayostahili maskini wako wanapokuwa na shauri.
sw.R: Maskini wa kwenu wanapokwenda mahakamani, usiipindishe sheria dhidi yao.

decisions.choice: turn aside the justice of your needy: deny the poor the verdict they are owed
decisions.reason: To turn justice aside is to bend a case away from what is right (Deuteronomy 16:19; 24:17; Amos 5:12). "Your needy" are the poor of your own people. Verse 3 kept the court from favoring the poor; this verse keeps it from wronging them.

decisions.choice: your poor / poor people among you
decisions.reason: "Your needy one" is collective; Balanced and Readable use the plural.

source.text: מִדְּבַר־שֶׁ֖קֶר תִּרְחָ֑ק וְנָקִ֤י וְצַדִּיק֙ אַֽל־תַּהֲרֹ֔ג כִּ֥י לֹא־אַצְדִּ֖יק רָשָֽׁע׃

records.literal_gloss: From a word of falsehood you will be distant, and an innocent [person] and a righteous [person] do not kill, for not I will declare righteous a wicked [person].

en.L: From a false matter you shall keep far; and the innocent and the righteous do not kill, for I will not justify the wicked.
en.B: Stay far away from a false charge. Do not put to death one who is innocent and in the right, for I will not declare the wicked to be in the right.
en.R: Have nothing to do with lies in court. Do not cause the death of an innocent person who has done nothing wrong. I will not treat the guilty as if they were innocent.

es.L: De palabra falsa te alejarás; y al inocente y al justo no mates, porque yo no justificaré al malvado.
es.B: Te mantendrás lejos de toda acusación falsa. No darás muerte al que es inocente y está en su derecho, porque yo no declararé justo al malvado.
es.R: No tengas nada que ver con mentiras en un juicio. No causes la muerte de una persona inocente que no ha hecho nada malo. Yo no trataré al culpable como si fuera inocente.

fr.L: D’une parole mensongère tu te tiendras loin ; et l’innocent et le juste, ne les tue pas, car je ne justifierai pas le méchant.
fr.B: Tu te tiendras loin de toute accusation mensongère. Tu ne feras pas mourir celui qui est innocent et qui a le droit pour lui, car je ne déclarerai pas juste le méchant.
fr.R: Ne te mêle pas aux mensonges dans un procès. Ne cause pas la mort d’un innocent qui n’a rien fait de mal. Je ne traiterai pas le coupable comme s’il était innocent.

sw.L: Jitenge mbali na neno la uongo; wala usimwue asiye na hatia na mwenye haki, kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} sitamhesabia haki mwovu.
sw.B: Ukae mbali na mashtaka ya uongo. Usimwue mtu asiye na hatia aliye na haki, kwa maana sitamtangaza mwovu kuwa na haki.
sw.R: Usihusike na uongo mahakamani. Usisababishe kifo cha mtu asiye na hatia ambaye hakufanya kosa lolote. Mimi sitamtendea mwenye hatia kana kwamba hana hatia.

decisions.choice: a false matter: a false charge or false testimony in a case
decisions.reason: The word can mean a word or a matter. In this setting it is a false accusation or a lying statement in court.

decisions.choice: do not kill the innocent: by a false case or an unjust verdict
decisions.reason: The innocent and the one in the right are killed here through the court, when false testimony or a bent judgment brings a death sentence (1 Kings 21:8-13).

decisions.choice: I will not justify the wicked: God's own judgment stands behind the court's
decisions.reason: The verb means to declare in the right, the language of a verdict. If a human court acquits the guilty, God will not (Proverbs 17:15; 34:7).

source.text: וְשֹׁ֖חַד לֹ֣א תִקָּ֑ח כִּ֤י הַשֹּׁ֨חַד֙ יְעַוֵּ֣ר פִּקְחִ֔ים וִֽיסַלֵּ֖ף דִּבְרֵ֥י צַדִּיקִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And a bribe not you must take, for the bribe makes blind clear-sighted [people] and perverts [the] words of righteous [people].

en.L: And a bribe you shall not take, for the bribe blinds the clear-sighted and subverts the words of the righteous.
en.B: Take no bribe. A bribe blinds the clear-sighted and overturns the cause of those who are in the right.
en.R: Never accept money or gifts to change your decision. Bribes keep even wise people from seeing clearly, and they twist the case of people who are in the right.

es.L: Y soborno no tomarás, porque el soborno ciega a los que ven claro y pervierte las palabras de los justos.
es.B: No aceptarás soborno. El soborno ciega a los que ven con claridad y trastorna la causa de los que tienen razón.
es.R: Nunca aceptes dinero ni regalos para cambiar tu decisión. Los sobornos impiden que incluso las personas sabias vean con claridad, y tuercen la causa de quienes tienen la razón.

fr.L: Et tu ne prendras pas de pot-de-vin, car le pot-de-vin aveugle les clairvoyants et fausse les paroles des justes.
fr.B: Tu n’accepteras pas de pot-de-vin. Le pot-de-vin aveugle ceux qui voient clair et renverse la cause de ceux qui sont dans leur droit.
fr.R: N’accepte jamais d’argent ou de cadeaux pour changer ta décision. Cela empêche même les sages de voir clair, et cela tord la cause des gens qui sont dans leur droit.

sw.L: Wala rushwa usipokee, kwa maana rushwa huwapofusha wenye kuona na kupotosha maneno ya wenye haki.
sw.B: Usipokee rushwa. Rushwa huwapofusha wanaoona vizuri na kupindua shauri la walio na haki.
sw.R: Kamwe usipokee pesa au zawadi ili ubadili uamuzi wako. Rushwa huwazuia hata watu wenye hekima wasione vizuri, na hupotosha shauri la watu walio na haki.

decisions.choice: blinds the clear-sighted: corrupts even those who see well
decisions.reason: The clear-sighted are those whose eyes are open: wise and fair judges. A bribe takes away the very sight they have (Deuteronomy 16:19).

decisions.choice: the words of the righteous: the case of those in the right
decisions.reason: The words of the righteous may be the pleas of the innocent party, which a bribe overturns, or the rulings of honest judges, which a bribe twists. The first fits the courtroom setting of verses 6-7.

decisions.choice: money or gifts to change your decision
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a bribe is.

source.text: וְגֵ֖ר לֹ֣א תִלְחָ֑ץ וְאַתֶּ֗ם יְדַעְתֶּם֙ אֶת־נֶ֣פֶשׁ הַגֵּ֔ר כִּֽי־גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And a sojourner not you must oppress, and you, you have known the life of the sojourner, for sojourners you were in [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: And a sojourner you shall not oppress; for you, you know the life of the sojourner, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.
en.B: Do not oppress a foreigner living among you. You know from the inside what a foreigner's life is like, since you yourselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
en.R: Do not be cruel to foreigners who live among you. You know what it is like to live in a land that is not your own. You lived that way in Egypt.

es.L: Y al extranjero no oprimirás; pues {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} la vida del extranjero, porque extranjeros {{plural_you:fueron|fuisteis}} en la tierra de Egipto.
es.B: No oprimirás al extranjero que vive en medio de ti. {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} por experiencia cómo es la vida del extranjero, pues también {{plural_you:fueron|fuisteis}} extranjeros en la tierra de Egipto.
es.R: No trates con crueldad a los extranjeros que viven contigo. {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} lo que es vivir en una tierra que no es la propia. Así {{plural_you:vivieron|vivisteis}} en Egipto.

fr.L: Et l’étranger, tu ne l’opprimeras pas ; vous, vous connaissez la vie de l’étranger, car vous avez été étrangers dans le pays d’Égypte.
fr.B: Tu n’opprimeras pas l’étranger qui vit chez toi. Vous savez de l’intérieur ce qu’est la vie d’un étranger, puisque vous-mêmes avez été étrangers au pays d’Égypte.
fr.R: Ne sois pas cruel avec les étrangers qui vivent chez toi. Vous savez ce que c’est de vivre dans un pays qui n’est pas le vôtre. C’est ce que vous avez vécu en Égypte.

sw.L: Wala mgeni usimwonee; kwa maana ninyi mnayajua maisha ya mgeni, kwa sababu mlikuwa wageni katika nchi ya Misri.
sw.B: Usimwonee mgeni anayeishi kwako. Ninyi mnajua kwa uzoefu wenu maisha ya mgeni yalivyo, kwa kuwa ninyi wenyewe mlikuwa wageni katika nchi ya Misri.
sw.R: Usiwe mkatili kwa wageni wanaoishi kwako. Mnajua jinsi ilivyo kuishi katika nchi isiyo yenu. Mliishi hivyo huko Misri.

decisions.choice: you know the life (soul) of the sojourner: you know from experience what it is to be one
decisions.reason: The word often rendered "soul" means the life or inner self of a person, with its needs and longings. Israel knows the stranger's life from within, having lived it in Egypt.

decisions.choice: the law of 22:20 repeated
decisions.reason: 22:20 gave the same command with the same reason. Here it closes the laws about the courts: a foreigner, who had no family to stand for him, must not be wronged in a case (Deuteronomy 24:17).

decisions.choice: foreigner living among you
decisions.reason: As in 12:19 and 12:48. Literal keeps "sojourner".

decisions.choice: singular "tú" for the commands, plural ({{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}) where the Hebrew turns to plural "you"
decisions.reason: The laws of chapters 21-23 mostly address Israel as one "you", but here (and in 23:13, 21, 25) the Hebrew turns to the plural. Spanish follows the Hebrew number, with plural_you spans on the plural forms; at Readable a sentence that begins in the plural stays plural.

decisions.choice: "tu" for the commands, "vous" where the Hebrew turns to plural "you"
decisions.reason: The laws mostly address Israel as one "you", but here (and in 23:13, 21, 25) the Hebrew turns to the plural. French follows the Hebrew number; at Readable a sentence that begins in the plural stays plural.

decisions.choice: singular "u-" for the commands, plural "ninyi", "m-" where the Hebrew turns to plural "you"
decisions.reason: The laws mostly address Israel as one "you", but here (and in 23:13, 21, 25) the Hebrew turns to the plural. Swahili marks the number in the verb and follows the Hebrew; at Readable a sentence that begins in the plural stays plural.

source.text: וְשֵׁ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים תִּזְרַ֣ע אֶת־אַרְצֶ֑ךָ וְאָסַפְתָּ֖ אֶת־תְּבוּאָתָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And six years you will sow your land and you will gather its produce,

en.L: And six years you shall sow your land and gather its produce,
en.B: For six years you are to sow your land and gather in its crops,
en.R: For six years, plant your fields and harvest the crops.

es.L: Y seis años sembrarás tu tierra y recogerás su producto,
es.B: Durante seis años sembrarás tu tierra y recogerás sus cosechas,
es.R: Durante seis años, siembra tus campos y recoge la cosecha.

fr.L: Et six années tu ensemenceras ta terre et tu en recueilleras le produit,
fr.B: Pendant six ans, tu sèmeras ta terre et tu en récolteras les fruits,
fr.R: Pendant six ans, sème tes champs et récolte ce qu’ils produisent.

sw.L: Na miaka sita utaipanda nchi yako na kuyavuna mazao yake,
sw.B: Kwa miaka sita utapanda mashamba yako na kuvuna mazao yake,
sw.R: Kwa miaka sita, panda mashamba yako na uvune mazao.

decisions.choice: six years: the pattern of the week applied to the land
decisions.reason: The six years of sowing and the seventh year of rest (verse 11) follow the six days of work and the seventh day of rest (verse 12; 20:9-10). Leviticus 25:1-7 gives the law of the land's Sabbath year at greater length.

source.text: וְהַשְּׁבִיעִ֞ת תִּשְׁמְטֶ֣נָּה וּנְטַשְׁתָּ֗הּ וְאָֽכְלוּ֙ אֶבְיֹנֵ֣י עַמֶּ֔ךָ וְיִתְרָ֕ם תֹּאכַ֖ל חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה כֵּֽן־תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה לְכַרְמְךָ֖ לְזֵיתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: and the seventh [year] you will let it rest and you will leave it fallow, and they will eat, the needy [people] of your people, and their excess will eat the animal[s] of the field. Thus you will do to your vineyard, to your olive grove.

en.L: but the seventh [year] you shall let it drop and leave it, and the needy of your people shall eat, and what they leave the animal[s] of the field shall eat. So you shall do to your vineyard, to your olive grove.
en.B: but in the seventh you are to release it and let it lie, so that the needy among your people may eat from it, and the wild animals may eat what they leave. Treat your vineyard and your olive grove the same way.
en.R: But in the seventh year, do not plant or harvest. Let the land rest. Poor people may eat whatever grows there, and wild animals may eat what is left. Do this with your grapevines and olive trees too.

es.L: pero el séptimo [año] la dejarás caer y la abandonarás, y comerán los necesitados de tu pueblo, y lo que ellos dejen lo comerán los animales del campo. Así harás con tu viña, con tu olivar.
es.B: pero el séptimo la dejarás libre y en reposo, para que coman de ella los necesitados de tu pueblo, y lo que ellos dejen lo coman los animales salvajes. Lo mismo harás con tu viña y con tu olivar.
es.R: Pero en el séptimo año no siembres ni coseches. Deja descansar la tierra. Los pobres podrán comer lo que crezca allí, y los animales salvajes podrán comer lo que sobre. Haz lo mismo con tus viñas y tus olivos.

fr.L: mais la septième [année] tu la laisseras tomber et tu l’abandonneras, et les indigents de ton peuple mangeront, et ce qu’ils laisseront, les bêtes des champs le mangeront. Ainsi tu feras pour ta vigne, pour ton oliveraie.
fr.B: mais la septième, tu la laisseras libre et en repos, afin que les pauvres de ton peuple en mangent, et que les bêtes sauvages mangent ce qu’ils laisseront. Tu feras de même pour ta vigne et ton oliveraie.
fr.R: Mais la septième année, ne sème pas et ne récolte pas. Laisse la terre se reposer. Les pauvres pourront manger tout ce qui y pousse, et les animaux sauvages mangeront ce qui reste. Fais la même chose avec tes vignes et tes oliviers.

sw.L: lakini [mwaka] wa saba utaiachilia na kuiacha, na maskini wa watu wako watakula, na kile watakachobakiza wanyama wa porini watakula. Ndivyo utakavyofanya kwa shamba lako la mizabibu, kwa shamba lako la mizeituni.
sw.B: lakini mwaka wa saba utaiachilia na kuiacha bila kulimwa, ili maskini miongoni mwa watu wako wapate kula, na wanyama wa porini wale kile watakachobakiza. Utafanya vivyo hivyo kwa shamba lako la mizabibu na la mizeituni.
sw.R: Lakini mwaka wa saba, usipande wala usivune. Iache ardhi ipumzike. Maskini wanaweza kula chochote kinachoota humo, na wanyama wa porini wanaweza kula kinachobaki. Fanya vivyo hivyo na mizabibu yako na mizeituni yako.

decisions.choice: let it drop and leave it: release the land from work and let it lie
decisions.reason: The first verb means to let fall or release; it is used of the release of debts in the seventh year (Deuteronomy 15:2). The second means to leave alone. The land is not sown, and what grows of itself is not harvested for the owner.

decisions.choice: the needy and the wild animals eat: the rest serves the poor and the creatures
decisions.reason: The seventh year is not only rest for the soil; what grows of itself belongs to the poor of the people, and what they leave to the animals (Leviticus 25:6-7).

decisions.choice: do not plant or harvest
decisions.reason: Readable says what letting the land rest means in practice.

source.text: שֵׁ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה מַעֲשֶׂ֔יךָ וּבַיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י תִּשְׁבֹּ֑ת לְמַ֣עַן יָנ֗וּחַ שֽׁוֹרְךָ֙ וַחֲמֹרֶ֔ךָ וְיִנָּפֵ֥שׁ בֶּן־אֲמָתְךָ֖ וְהַגֵּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Six days you will do your work(s), and on the day the seventh you will rest, so that it may rest, your ox and your donkey, and he will refresh himself, the child of your female slave and the sojourner.

en.L: Six days you shall do your works, and on the seventh day you shall cease, so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the {{gender:child|son}} of your slave woman and the sojourner may be refreshed.
en.B: Work for six days, but on the seventh day stop, so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the {{gender:child|son}} of your female servant and the foreigner living among you may be refreshed.
en.R: Do your work in six days, but stop working on the seventh day. Then your ox and your donkey can rest. The {{gender:child|son}} of your female servant and the foreigner who lives with you can rest and get their strength back.

es.L: Seis días harás tus obras, y en el día séptimo cesarás, para que descansen tu buey y tu asno, y tomen aliento el hijo de tu esclava y el extranjero.
es.B: Seis días trabajarás, pero el séptimo día te detendrás, para que descansen tu buey y tu asno, y recobren aliento el hijo de tu sierva y el extranjero que vive contigo.
es.R: Haz tu trabajo en seis días, pero el séptimo día deja de trabajar. Así podrán descansar tu buey y tu burro. También el hijo de tu sierva y el extranjero que vive contigo podrán descansar y recuperar fuerzas.

fr.L: Six jours tu feras tes ouvrages, et le septième jour tu cesseras, afin que se reposent ton bœuf et ton âne, et que reprennent haleine {{gender:l’enfant|le fils}} de ton esclave et l’étranger.
fr.B: Tu travailleras six jours, mais le septième jour tu t’arrêteras, pour que ton bœuf et ton âne se reposent, et que {{gender:l’enfant|le fils}} de ta servante et l’étranger qui vit chez toi reprennent souffle.
fr.R: Fais ton travail en six jours, mais le septième jour, arrête de travailler. Ainsi ton bœuf et ton âne pourront se reposer. {{gender:L’enfant|Le fils}} de ta servante et l’étranger qui vit chez toi pourront eux aussi se reposer et reprendre des forces.

sw.L: Siku sita utafanya kazi zako, na siku ya saba utaacha, ili wapumzike ng'ombe wako na punda wako, na wapate nafuu mwana wa mtumwa wako wa kike na mgeni.
sw.B: Utafanya kazi siku sita, lakini siku ya saba utaacha, ili ng'ombe wako na punda wako wapumzike, na mwana wa mtumishi wako wa kike na mgeni anayeishi kwako wapate kuburudika.
sw.R: Fanya kazi yako kwa siku sita, lakini siku ya saba acha kufanya kazi. Hapo ng'ombe wako na punda wako wataweza kupumzika. Mwana wa mtumishi wako wa kike na mgeni anayeishi kwako nao wataweza kupumzika na kupata nguvu tena.

decisions.choice: six days ... on the seventh day you shall cease: the Sabbath command repeated
decisions.reason: The verb is the one from which the word Sabbath comes. The command of 20:8-11 is given again here, with its reason turned toward the weak: the animals, the slave and the foreigner.

decisions.choice: be refreshed: catch one's breath, be revived
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for breath or life. It is used of God himself resting on the seventh day (31:17) and of a weary man reviving (2 Samuel 16:14).

decisions.choice: the son of your slave woman: a slave born in the household
decisions.reason: The son of a slave woman was himself born a slave in the household (Genesis 14:14; Psalm 116:16). He, too, is given the day of rest.

decisions.choice: female servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave". The meaning decision (m3) keeps that her son was born a slave in the household.

source.text: וּבְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־אָמַ֥רְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם תִּשָּׁמֵ֑רוּ וְשֵׁ֨ם אֱלֹהִ֤ים אֲחֵרִים֙ לֹ֣א תַזְכִּ֔ירוּ לֹ֥א יִשָּׁמַ֖ע עַל־פִּֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And in all that I have said to you, you will take heed; and [the] name of other gods not you will bring to remembrance; not it will be heard on your mouth.

en.L: And in all that I have said to you take heed; and the name of other gods you shall not mention; it shall not be heard on your mouth.
en.B: Be on guard in all that I have said to you. Do not make mention of the names of other gods; let no such name be heard from your mouth.
en.R: Be careful to obey everything I have told you. Do not pray to other gods or even say their names.

es.L: Y en todo lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} he dicho {{plural_you:estarán|estaréis}} atentos; y el nombre de otros dioses no {{plural_you:mencionarán|mencionaréis}}; no se oirá en tu boca.
es.B: {{plural_you:Estarán|Estaréis}} atentos a todo lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} he dicho. No {{plural_you:mencionarán|mencionaréis}} los nombres de otros dioses; que ninguno de esos nombres se oiga de tu boca.
es.R: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} cuidado de obedecer todo lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} he dicho. No {{plural_you:oren|oréis}} a otros dioses, y ni siquiera {{plural_you:digan|digáis}} sus nombres.

fr.L: Et dans tout ce que je vous ai dit, vous prendrez garde ; et le nom d’autres dieux, vous ne l’évoquerez pas ; on ne l’entendra pas dans ta bouche.
fr.B: Vous prendrez garde à tout ce que je vous ai dit. Vous ne ferez pas mention du nom d’autres dieux ; qu’aucun de ces noms ne sorte de ta bouche.
fr.R: Faites bien attention à obéir à tout ce que je vous ai dit. Ne priez pas d’autres dieux, et ne prononcez même pas leur nom.

sw.L: Na katika yote niliyowaambia mtajihadhari; na jina la miungu mingine msilitaje; lisisikike kinywani mwako.
sw.B: Mjihadhari katika yote niliyowaambia. Msiyataje majina ya miungu mingine; jina kama hilo lisisikike kinywani mwako.
sw.R: Mwe waangalifu kutii kila kitu nilichowaambia. Msiiombe miungu mingine, wala msiyataje hata majina yake.

decisions.choice: do not make mention of the name of other gods: do not call on them or speak of them with honor
decisions.reason: To "cause to remember" a name is to call on it, swear by it or praise it (Joshua 23:7; Psalm 20:8). Israel is not to call on other gods in worship or oath; the command guards the first commandment (20:3).

decisions.choice: in all that I have said: the whole of the law just given
decisions.reason: The sentence closes the laws of 20:22-23:12 before the laws of the feasts. Heeding all that God has said comes first; turning from other gods sums it up.

decisions.choice: pray to ... or even say their names
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what making mention of a god's name involves: calling on it in prayer, and speaking it at all.

source.text: שָׁלֹ֣שׁ רְגָלִ֔ים תָּחֹ֥ג לִ֖י בַּשָּׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Three feet you will celebrate a festival to me in the year.

en.L: Three times you shall keep a feast to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the year.
en.B: Three times each year you shall keep a pilgrim feast in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} honor.
en.R: Each year you must hold three festivals to honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Tres veces celebrarás fiesta para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} en el año.
es.B: Tres veces al año celebrarás una fiesta de peregrinación en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} honor.
es.R: Cada año debes celebrar tres fiestas en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} honor.

fr.L: Trois fois tu célébreras une fête pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} dans l’année.
fr.B: Trois fois par an, tu célébreras une fête de pèlerinage en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} honneur.
fr.R: Chaque année, tu dois célébrer trois fêtes en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} honneur.

sw.L: Mara tatu utafanya sikukuu kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} katika mwaka.
sw.B: Mara tatu kila mwaka utaadhimisha sikukuu ya safari ya ibada kwa heshima {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.
sw.R: Kila mwaka lazima uadhimishe sikukuu tatu kwa heshima {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.

decisions.choice: three feet: three times
decisions.reason: The word for "feet" is used here for "times" (Numbers 22:28), perhaps because each feast meant a journey on foot to the place of worship. Verse 17 says the same with the usual word for "times".

decisions.choice: keep a feast: hold a pilgrim festival
decisions.reason: The verb means to hold a festival, often with a journey to the sanctuary; it is the verb Moses used when asking Pharaoh to let the people go to hold a feast in the wilderness (5:1; 10:9).

decisions.choice: pilgrim feast
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "pilgrim" to show that these feasts were kept by going to worship at the sanctuary (verse 17).

decisions.choice: sikukuu ya safari ya ibada (a feast of a journey for worship)
decisions.reason: "Hija" is the usual Swahili word for a pilgrimage, but it names above all the Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca. Balanced describes the journey to worship instead.

source.text: אֶת־חַ֣ג הַמַּצּוֹת֮ תִּשְׁמֹר֒ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִים֩ תֹּאכַ֨ל מַצּ֜וֹת כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֗ךָ לְמוֹעֵד֙ חֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽאָבִ֔יב כִּי־ב֖וֹ יָצָ֣אתָ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וְלֹא־יֵרָא֥וּ פָנַ֖י רֵיקָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: The festival of the unleavened bread(s) you will keep; seven days you will eat unleavened bread(s), just as I commanded you, at the appointed time [of] the month of Abib, for in it you came out from Egypt. And not they will present themselves [before] my presence empty.

en.L: The Feast of Unleavened Bread you shall keep; seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time [in] the month of Abib, for in it you came out from Egypt. And none shall appear before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} empty.
en.B: Observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread: you shall eat unleavened bread seven days, as I instructed you, at its fixed time in the month of Abib, the month when you left Egypt. And let no one come into {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence empty-handed.
en.R: First, celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days, eat unleavened bread made without yeast, as I told you. Do this at the time I set in the month of Abib, in early spring, because that is when you left Egypt. Everyone who comes before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} must bring a gift.

es.L: La fiesta de los Panes sin Levadura guardarás; siete días comerás panes sin levadura, como te mandé, al tiempo señalado del mes de Abib, porque en él saliste de Egipto. Y no se presentarán vacíos ante {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.B: Guardarás la fiesta de los Panes sin Levadura: siete días comerás pan sin levadura, como te he ordenado, en su fecha fija del mes de Abib, el mes en que saliste de Egipto. Y nadie se presentará ante {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} con las manos vacías.
es.R: Primero, celebra la fiesta de los Panes sin Levadura. Durante siete días, come pan hecho sin levadura, como te dije. Hazlo en la fecha que fijé en el mes de Abib, a comienzos de la primavera, porque en ese mes saliste de Egipto. Todo el que venga ante {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} debe traer una ofrenda.

fr.L: La fête des Pains sans levain, tu l’observeras ; sept jours tu mangeras des pains sans levain, comme je te l’ai ordonné, au temps fixé du mois d’Abib, car en [ce mois] tu es sorti d’Égypte. Et on ne paraîtra pas devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} à vide.
fr.B: Tu observeras la fête des Pains sans levain : pendant sept jours tu mangeras des pains sans levain, comme je te l’ai prescrit, à la date fixée du mois d’Abib, le mois où tu es sorti d’Égypte. Et personne ne se présentera devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} les mains vides.
fr.R: D’abord, célèbre la fête des Pains sans levain. Pendant sept jours, mange du pain fait sans levain, comme je te l’ai dit. Fais-le au moment que j’ai fixé, au mois d’Abib, au début du printemps, parce que c’est à ce moment-là que tu es sorti d’Égypte. Toute personne qui vient devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} doit apporter un don.

sw.L: Sikukuu ya Mikate Isiyotiwa Chachu utaishika; siku saba utakula mikate isiyotiwa chachu, kama nilivyokuamuru, kwa wakati ulioamriwa wa mwezi wa Abibu, kwa maana ndani yake ulitoka Misri. Wala wasionekane mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} mikono mitupu.
sw.B: Utaishika Sikukuu ya Mikate Isiyotiwa Chachu: siku saba utakula mikate isiyotiwa chachu, kama nilivyokuagiza, kwa wakati wake uliowekwa katika mwezi wa Abibu, mwezi ule ulipotoka Misri. Na mtu yeyote asije mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} mikono mitupu.
sw.R: Kwanza, adhimisha Sikukuu ya Mikate Isiyotiwa Chachu. Kwa siku saba, kula mikate iliyotengenezwa bila chachu, kama nilivyokuambia. Fanya hivyo wakati niliouweka katika mwezi wa Abibu, mwanzoni mwa majira ya kuchipua, kwa sababu ndio wakati ulipotoka Misri. Kila anayekuja mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} lazima alete zawadi.

decisions.choice: the Feast of Unleavened Bread in Abib: the feast commanded in 12:15-20 and 13:3-10
decisions.reason: Abib, "fresh ears of grain", is the spring month in which Israel left Egypt (13:4). The seven days of unleavened bread follow the Passover (12:15-20).

decisions.choice: none shall appear before me empty: no one is to come to worship without an offering
alternatives: none shall see my face empty-handed
decisions.reason: The verb form as the Hebrew text is pointed means "be seen" or "appear" before God's face. The same consonants could be read "see my face", and some think that was the first reading, later softened. Either way the worshiper comes into God's presence and must not come with nothing to offer (34:20; Deuteronomy 16:16-17).

decisions.choice: First ... in early spring
decisions.reason: Readable numbers the three feasts of verses 15-16 and places Abib in the year, as in 13:4.

source.text: וְחַ֤ג הַקָּצִיר֙ בִּכּוּרֵ֣י מַעֲשֶׂ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּזְרַ֖ע בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה וְחַ֤ג הָֽאָסִף֙ בְּצֵ֣את הַשָּׁנָ֔ה בְּאָסְפְּךָ֥ אֶֽת־מַעֲשֶׂ֖יךָ מִן־הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the festival of the harvest, the first-fruits of your works which you will sow in [the] field, and the festival of the ingathering when goes out the year, when you have gathered your works from the field.

en.L: And the Feast of Harvest, the firstfruits of your works, which you sow in the field; and the Feast of Ingathering at the going out of the year, when you gather in your works from the field.
en.B: Keep also the Feast of Harvest, with the firstfruits of your labor, of what you sow in the field, and the Feast of Ingathering at the turn of the year, when you gather in from the field what your labor has produced.
en.R: Second, celebrate the Festival of Harvest when the first crops you planted are ready. Third, celebrate the Festival of Ingathering at the end of the growing year, when you bring in your crops from the fields.

es.L: Y la fiesta de la Siega, de las primicias de tus labores, de lo que siembres en el campo; y la fiesta de la Recolección a la salida del año, cuando recojas tus labores del campo.
es.B: Guardarás también la fiesta de la Siega, con las primicias de tu trabajo, de lo que siembres en el campo, y la fiesta de la Recolección al cerrarse el año, cuando recojas del campo el fruto de tu trabajo.
es.R: Segundo, celebra la fiesta de la Siega cuando estén listas las primeras cosechas que sembraste. Tercero, celebra la fiesta de la Recolección al final del año agrícola, cuando recojas las cosechas de tus campos.

fr.L: Et la fête de la Moisson, des prémices de tes travaux, de ce que tu sèmeras dans le champ ; et la fête de la Récolte à la sortie de l’année, quand tu recueilleras tes travaux du champ.
fr.B: Tu célébreras aussi la fête de la Moisson, avec les prémices de ton travail, de ce que tu as semé dans les champs, et la fête de la Récolte au tournant de l’année, quand tu rentreras des champs le fruit de ton travail.
fr.R: Ensuite, célèbre la fête de la Moisson quand les premières récoltes que tu as semées sont prêtes. Enfin, célèbre la fête de la Récolte à la fin de l’année agricole, quand tu rentres tes récoltes des champs.

sw.L: Na sikukuu ya Mavuno, malimbuko ya kazi zako, unazopanda shambani; na sikukuu ya Kukusanya Mazao wakati mwaka unapotoka, unapokusanya kazi zako kutoka shambani.
sw.B: Pia utaishika Sikukuu ya Mavuno, kwa malimbuko ya kazi yako, ya kile unachopanda shambani, na Sikukuu ya Kukusanya Mazao mwaka unapogeuka, unapokusanya kutoka shambani mazao ya kazi yako.
sw.R: Pili, adhimisha Sikukuu ya Mavuno mazao ya kwanza uliyopanda yanapokuwa tayari. Tatu, adhimisha Sikukuu ya Kukusanya Mazao mwishoni mwa mwaka wa kilimo, unapoleta mazao yako kutoka mashambani.

decisions.choice: the Feast of Harvest: the wheat harvest, later called the Feast of Weeks
decisions.reason: This is the feast of the first of the grain harvest, called the Feast of Weeks in 34:22 and Deuteronomy 16:9-10, seven weeks after the start of the harvest (Leviticus 23:15-17).

decisions.choice: the Feast of Ingathering at the going out of the year: the autumn feast, later called Booths
decisions.reason: The last harvest of fruit, grapes and olives was gathered in autumn, at the close of the farming year. The feast is called the Feast of Booths in Leviticus 23:34-43 and Deuteronomy 16:13. "The going out of the year" means the end of the year's work in the fields; 34:22 calls it "the turn of the year".

decisions.choice: Second ... Third ... growing year
decisions.reason: Readable numbers the feasts and makes clear that the year meant is the farming year.

decisions.choice: la fiesta de la Siega; la fiesta de la Recolección
alternatives: la fiesta de la Cosecha; la fiesta de las Cosechas
decisions.reason: Two harvest words are needed: "Siega" (reaping) for the grain harvest, "Recolección" (gathering in) for the autumn feast, so the names stay distinct.

decisions.choice: la fête de la Moisson; la fête de la Récolte
decisions.reason: "Moisson" is the grain harvest; "Récolte" names the autumn gathering of fruit, grapes and olives, keeping the two feasts distinct.

decisions.choice: Sikukuu ya Mavuno; Sikukuu ya Kukusanya Mazao
decisions.reason: "Mavuno" is the harvest; the autumn feast is named for the gathering in of the crops, as the Hebrew name says.

source.text: שָׁלֹ֥שׁ פְּעָמִ֖ים בַּשָּׁנָ֑ה יֵרָאֶה֙ כָּל־זְכ֣וּרְךָ֔ אֶל־פְּנֵ֖י הָאָדֹ֥ן׀יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Three times in the year he will present himself, every male of yours, to the presence of the lord Yahweh.

en.L: Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the face of the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Three times a year every male among you is to present himself before the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Three times every year, all your men and boys must come and stand before the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Tres veces en el año se presentará todo varón tuyo ante el rostro del Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Tres veces al año todos tus varones se presentarán ante el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Tres veces cada año, todos tus hombres y muchachos deben venir a presentarse ante el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Trois fois dans l’année, tout mâle chez toi paraîtra devant la face du Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Trois fois par an, tous tes hommes se présenteront devant le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Trois fois chaque année, tous les hommes et les garçons doivent venir se présenter devant le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Mara tatu katika mwaka kila mwanamume wako ataonekana mbele ya uso wa Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Mara tatu kwa mwaka kila mwanamume miongoni mwako atajihudhurisha mbele ya Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Mara tatu kila mwaka, wanaume wako wote na wavulana lazima waje kusimama mbele ya Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: the Lord Yahweh: the divine name with the title "Lord" before it
decisions.reason: "Lord" is the title of a master or sovereign; joined to the divine name it calls Yahweh Israel's master, to whom the people come as servants three times a year (34:23).

decisions.choice: all your males: the men were required to come
decisions.reason: The duty to come to the sanctuary was laid on the males. Women and children often came as well (Deuteronomy 16:11, 14; 1 Samuel 1:3-7).

decisions.choice: the Lord GOD
decisions.reason: Where the title "Lord" comes just before the divine name, "GOD" in capitals marks the name, to avoid "Lord LORD".

source.text: לֹֽא־תִזְבַּ֥ח עַל־חָמֵ֖ץ דַּם־זִבְחִ֑י וְלֹֽא־יָלִ֥ין חֵֽלֶב־חַגִּ֖י עַד־בֹּֽקֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: Not you must sacrifice with leaven the blood of my sacrifice, and not it will remain overnight, the fat of my festival sacrifice, until morning.

en.L: You shall not sacrifice the blood of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sacrifice with leaven; and the fat of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feast shall not remain overnight until morning.
en.B: Do not offer the blood of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sacrifice with anything leavened, and the fat from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feast must not be left over until morning.
en.R: When you offer an animal to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, do not offer bread made with yeast along with its blood. And do not keep the fat from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} festival sacrifices until the next morning.

es.L: No sacrificarás con levadura la sangre de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} sacrificio, y no pasará la noche la grasa de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} fiesta hasta la mañana.
es.B: No ofrecerás la sangre de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} sacrificio junto con nada que tenga levadura, y la grasa de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} fiesta no se dejará hasta la mañana.
es.R: Cuando {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ofrezcas un animal, no ofrezcas con su sangre pan hecho con levadura. Y no guardes hasta la mañana siguiente la grasa de los sacrificios de {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} fiestas.

fr.L: Tu ne sacrifieras pas avec du levain le sang de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} sacrifice, et la graisse de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fête ne passera pas la nuit jusqu’au matin.
fr.B: Tu n’offriras pas le sang de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} sacrifice avec du pain levé, et la graisse de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fête ne sera pas gardée jusqu’au matin.
fr.R: Quand tu {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}offres un animal, n’offre pas avec son sang du pain fait avec du levain. Et ne garde pas jusqu’au lendemain matin la graisse des sacrifices de {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} fêtes.

sw.L: Usitoe damu ya dhabihu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} pamoja na chachu, wala mafuta ya sikukuu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} yasikae usiku kucha mpaka asubuhi.
sw.B: Usitoe damu ya dhabihu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} pamoja na kitu chochote kilichotiwa chachu, na mafuta ya sikukuu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} yasibaki mpaka asubuhi.
sw.R: Unaponitolea mnyama kuwa sadaka, usitoe pamoja na damu yake mkate uliotiwa chachu. Wala usiyaweke mpaka asubuhi inayofuata mafuta ya dhabihu za sikukuu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}.

decisions.choice: the blood of my sacrifice with leaven: no leavened bread with a blood sacrifice
decisions.reason: Leaven was kept away from the altar (Leviticus 2:11). In 34:25 the same law is tied to the Passover sacrifice, which was eaten with unleavened bread (12:8).

decisions.choice: the fat of my feast: the fat of the festival sacrifice
decisions.reason: "My feast" stands for the sacrifice offered at the feast. Its fat belonged to God and was to be burned on the altar the same night, not left over (Leviticus 3:16; 7:15). In 34:25 the parallel speaks of the Passover sacrifice.

decisions.choice: When you offer an animal to me ... bread made with yeast
decisions.reason: Readable explains the sacrifice and the leaven.

source.text: רֵאשִׁ֗ית בִּכּוּרֵי֙ אַדְמָ֣תְךָ֔ תָּבִ֕יא בֵּ֖ית יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לֹֽא־תְבַשֵּׁ֥ל גְּדִ֖י בַּחֲלֵ֥ב אִמּֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: The first of the first-fruits of your ground you will bring [to] the house of Yahweh your God. Not you must boil a kid in the milk of its mother.

en.L: The first of the firstfruits of your ground you shall bring [to the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk.
en.B: The best of your ground's firstfruits you are to bring to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
en.R: Bring the best of the first crops from your land to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Do not cook a young goat in milk from its own mother.

es.L: Lo primero de las primicias de tu tierra traerás [a la] casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} tu Dios. No cocerás un cabrito en la leche de su madre.
es.B: Lo mejor de las primicias de tu tierra lo llevarás a la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} tu Dios. No cocerás un cabrito en la leche de su madre.
es.R: Lleva lo mejor de las primeras cosechas de tu tierra a la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} tu Dios. No cocines un cabrito en la leche de su propia madre.

fr.L: Les premières des prémices de ton sol, tu [les] apporteras [à la] maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ton Dieu. Tu ne feras pas cuire un chevreau dans le lait de sa mère.
fr.B: Tu apporteras à la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ton Dieu le meilleur des prémices de ton sol. Tu ne feras pas cuire un chevreau dans le lait de sa mère.
fr.R: Apporte le meilleur des premières récoltes de ta terre à la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ton Dieu. Ne fais pas cuire un jeune chevreau dans le lait de sa propre mère.

sw.L: Malimbuko ya kwanza ya ardhi yako utayaleta [katika] nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako. Usimtokose mwanambuzi katika maziwa ya mama yake.
sw.B: Malimbuko bora ya ardhi yako utayaleta katika nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako. Usimtokose mwanambuzi katika maziwa ya mama yake.
sw.R: Leta mazao bora ya kwanza ya ardhi yako katika nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako. Usimpike mwanambuzi katika maziwa ya mama yake mwenyewe.

decisions.choice: the first of the firstfruits: the best and earliest of the crop
decisions.reason: The first word can mean the first in time or the first in quality, the best (Numbers 18:12). Both senses fit: the earliest and choicest produce belongs to God.

decisions.choice: the house of Yahweh: the place where God is worshiped
decisions.reason: No temple yet existed. The house of Yahweh is the sanctuary God will choose, first the tabernacle (25:8) and later the temple (Deuteronomy 26:2).

decisions.choice: do not boil a young goat in its mother's milk: the reason is uncertain
decisions.reason: The law is given three times (here; 34:26; Deuteronomy 14:21) with no reason stated. It may forbid a practice of other peoples' worship, or it may teach respect for the bond between mother and young, like Leviticus 22:28 and Deuteronomy 22:6-7. Its placement here, with the firstfruits, ties it to the harvest feasts.

source.text: הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י שֹׁלֵ֤חַ מַלְאָךְ֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ לִשְׁמָרְךָ֖ בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ וְלַהֲבִ֣יאֲךָ֔ אֶל־הַמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֲכִנֹֽתִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Here! I [am] about to send an angel before you to guard you on the journey and to bring you into the place which I have prepared.

en.L: Look, I am sending an angel before you to guard you on the way and to bring you into the place that I have prepared.
en.B: I am sending an angel to go before you. He will protect you on your journey and lead you to the place I have made ready.
en.R: I am sending an angel in front of you. He will keep you safe on the road and bring you to the place I have made ready for you.

es.L: Mira, yo envío un ángel delante de ti para que te guarde en el camino y te lleve al lugar que he preparado.
es.B: Yo envío un ángel que irá delante de ti. Él te protegerá en el viaje y te conducirá al lugar que he dispuesto.
es.R: Voy a enviar un ángel delante de ti. Él te cuidará en el camino y te llevará al lugar que he preparado para ti.

fr.L: Voici, j’envoie un ange devant toi pour te garder en chemin et pour te faire entrer dans le lieu que j’ai préparé.
fr.B: J’envoie un ange qui marchera devant toi. Il te protégera pendant ton voyage et te conduira au lieu que j’ai préparé.
fr.R: Je vais envoyer un ange devant toi. Il te gardera en sécurité sur la route et t’amènera à l’endroit que j’ai préparé pour toi.

sw.L: Tazama, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninamtuma malaika mbele yako akulinde njiani na kukuleta mahali nilipoandaa.
sw.B: Ninamtuma malaika atangulie mbele yako. Atakulinda katika safari yako na kukuongoza mpaka mahali nilipoandaa.
sw.R: Ninamtuma malaika akutangulie. Atakulinda njiani na kukufikisha mahali nilipokuandalia.

decisions.choice: an angel (messenger): a messenger sent by God
decisions.reason: The word means a messenger, human or heavenly. Here it is God's messenger who goes before Israel, as "the angel of God" went before the camp at the sea (14:19). In 32:34 and 33:2 God again promises to send an angel before them.

decisions.choice: the place I have prepared: the land of Canaan
decisions.reason: The place is the land God promised (verse 23; 3:8). Moses' song speaks of the place God made for his dwelling (15:17).

decisions.choice: "Look" left out
decisions.reason: Balanced drops "look" here and begins with God's announcement; Literal keeps it.

source.text: הִשָּׁ֧מֶר מִפָּנָ֛יו וּשְׁמַ֥ע בְּקֹל֖וֹ אַל־תַּמֵּ֣ר בּ֑וֹ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יִשָּׂא֙ לְפִשְׁעֲכֶ֔ם כִּ֥י שְׁמִ֖י בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Take care before him and listen to his voice; do not cause bitterness in him, for not he will forgive your transgression, for my name [is] within him.

en.L: Take heed before him and listen to his voice; do not rebel against him, for he will not pardon your transgression, for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name [is] in him.
en.B: Take care in his presence and obey what he says. Do not defy him, because he will not pardon your wrongdoing; {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is in him.
en.R: Be careful to respect him and do what he tells you. Do not turn against him. He will not overlook your sins, because {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is in him.

es.L: Guárdate delante de él y escucha su voz; no te rebeles contra él, porque no perdonará la transgresión de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, pues {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre [está] en él.
es.B: Ten cuidado en su presencia y obedece lo que dice. No lo desafíes, porque no perdonará la rebeldía de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre está en él.
es.R: Ten cuidado de respetarlo y de hacer lo que te diga. No te pongas en su contra. Él no pasará por alto tus pecados, porque {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre está en él.

fr.L: Prends garde devant lui et écoute sa voix ; ne te révolte pas contre lui, car il ne pardonnera pas votre transgression, car {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom [est] en lui.
fr.B: Sois attentif en sa présence et obéis à ce qu’il dit. Ne le défie pas, car il ne pardonnera pas votre faute ; {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom est en lui.
fr.R: Fais attention à le respecter et à faire ce qu’il te dit. Ne te retourne pas contre lui. Il ne fermera pas les yeux sur tes péchés, parce que {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom est en lui.

sw.L: Jihadhari mbele yake, uisikilize sauti yake; usimwasi, kwa maana hatawasamehe makosa yenu, kwa kuwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} [limo] ndani yake.
sw.B: Uwe mwangalifu mbele yake na kutii anachosema. Usimkaidi, kwa maana hatawasamehe uasi wenu; jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} limo ndani yake.
sw.R: Uwe mwangalifu kumheshimu na kufanya anachokuambia. Usimgeuke. Hatapuuza dhambi zako, kwa sababu jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} limo ndani yake.

decisions.choice: do not rebel against him: do not provoke or defy him
decisions.reason: The verb is from a root meaning to be bitter or to rebel; to embitter someone is to provoke him by defiance. Israel would do this in the wilderness (Psalm 78:40, 56).

decisions.choice: my name is in him: he bears God's own presence and authority
decisions.reason: God's name stands for God himself as he makes himself known (3:15; 20:24). The angel acts with God's full authority and presence, so to defy him is to defy God. Some see in this angel God himself appearing (compare 3:2-6; 33:14-15); the verse does not say.

decisions.choice: he will not pardon your transgression: rebellion will not be passed over
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift or bear, here to forgive. The warning is that defying the angel is defying God.

source.text: כִּ֣י אִם־שָׁמֹ֤עַ תִּשְׁמַע֙ בְּקֹל֔וֹ וְעָשִׂ֕יתָ כֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲדַבֵּ֑ר וְאָֽיַבְתִּי֙ אֶת־אֹ֣יְבֶ֔יךָ וְצַרְתִּ֖י אֶת־צֹרְרֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: For if carefully you will listen to his voice and you will do all that I will say, and I will be an enemy to your enemies and I will treat as a foe your foes.

en.L: For if you surely listen to his voice and do all that I say, then I will be an enemy to your enemies and a foe to your foes.
en.B: If you truly heed his voice and do everything I tell you, then I will be an enemy to your enemies and an adversary to those who stand against you.
en.R: If you listen closely to him and do all I tell you, I will fight against your enemies and stand against all who attack you.

es.L: Porque si de veras escuchas su voz y haces todo lo que yo digo, seré enemigo de tus enemigos y adversario de tus adversarios.
es.B: Si de verdad obedeces su voz y haces todo lo que te digo, entonces seré enemigo de tus enemigos y adversario de los que se levanten contra ti.
es.R: Si lo escuchas con atención y haces todo lo que te digo, yo pelearé contra tus enemigos y me pondré en contra de todos los que te ataquen.

fr.L: Car si tu écoutes vraiment sa voix et fais tout ce que je dis, je serai l’ennemi de tes ennemis et l’adversaire de tes adversaires.
fr.B: Si tu obéis fidèlement à sa voix et fais tout ce que je te dis, alors je serai l’ennemi de tes ennemis et l’adversaire de ceux qui se dressent contre toi.
fr.R: Si tu l’écoutes bien et fais tout ce que je te dis, je combattrai tes ennemis et je m’opposerai à tous ceux qui t’attaquent.

sw.L: Kwa maana ukiisikiliza kweli sauti yake na kufanya yote ninayosema, nitakuwa adui wa adui zako na mpinzani wa wapinzani wako.
sw.B: Ukiitii kweli sauti yake na kufanya kila ninachokuambia, nitakuwa adui wa adui zako na mpinzani wa wale wanaosimama dhidi yako.
sw.R: Ukimsikiliza kwa makini na kufanya yote ninayokuambia, nitapigana na adui zako na kuwapinga wote wanaokushambulia.

decisions.choice: listen to his voice ... all that I say: the angel's word is God's word
decisions.reason: Obeying the angel's voice is doing what God says; the two are one (verse 21).

decisions.choice: I will be an enemy to your enemies: God takes Israel's side
decisions.reason: The promise echoes God's word to Abraham (Genesis 12:3). The two verbs are a pair: Israel's enemies and foes become God's.

source.text: כִּֽי־יֵלֵ֣ךְ מַלְאָכִי֮ לְפָנֶיךָ֒ וֶהֱבִֽיאֲךָ֗ אֶל־הָֽאֱמֹרִי֙ וְהַ֣חִתִּ֔י וְהַפְּרִזִּי֙ וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י הַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִ֑י וְהִכְחַדְתִּֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: For he will go, my angel, before you and he will bring you to the Amorite[s] and the Hittite[s] and the Perizzite[s] and the Canaanite[s], the Hivite[s] and the Jebusite[s], and I will annihilate it.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} angel will go before you and bring you to the Amorites and the Hittites and the Perizzites and the Canaanites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, and I will wipe them out.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} angel will go before you and bring you to the land of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, and I will make an end of them.
en.R: My angel will lead you into the land where the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites and Jebusites live. And I will destroy those nations.

es.L: Porque {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ángel irá delante de ti y te llevará a los amorreos, a los hititas, a los ferezeos, a los cananeos, a los heveos y a los jebuseos, y yo los exterminaré.
es.B: Porque {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ángel irá delante de ti y te llevará a la tierra de los amorreos, los hititas, los ferezeos, los cananeos, los heveos y los jebuseos, y yo acabaré con ellos.
es.R: Mi ángel te guiará hasta la tierra donde viven los amorreos, los hititas, los ferezeos, los cananeos, los heveos y los jebuseos. Y yo destruiré a esas naciones.

fr.L: Car {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} ange ira devant toi et te conduira vers les Amoréens, les Hittites, les Phéréziens, les Cananéens, les Héviens et les Jébusiens, et je les effacerai.
fr.B: Car {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} ange marchera devant toi et te conduira au pays des Amoréens, des Hittites, des Phéréziens, des Cananéens, des Héviens et des Jébusiens, et j’en finirai avec eux.
fr.R: Mon ange te conduira dans le pays où vivent les Amoréens, les Hittites, les Phéréziens, les Cananéens, les Héviens et les Jébusiens. Et je détruirai ces peuples.

sw.L: Kwa maana malaika {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} atakwenda mbele yako na kukuleta kwa Waamori, na Wahiti, na Waperizi, na Wakanaani, Wahivi na Wayebusi, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitawafutilia mbali.
sw.B: Kwa maana malaika {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} atakutangulia na kukuleta katika nchi ya Waamori, Wahiti, Waperizi, Wakanaani, Wahivi na Wayebusi, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitawakomesha.
sw.R: Malaika {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} atakuongoza mpaka nchi wanamoishi Waamori, Wahiti, Waperizi, Wakanaani, Wahivi na Wayebusi. Nami nitayaangamiza mataifa hayo.

decisions.choice: the peoples of Canaan: the nations named in the promise to the fathers
decisions.reason: The list repeats the peoples named when God first spoke to Moses (3:8, 17; compare Genesis 15:19-21).

decisions.choice: I will wipe them out: I will destroy them as nations
decisions.reason: The verb means to cut off or efface. Its object is singular, gathering the nations into one. Verses 28-30 show this done by driving them out little by little.

decisions.choice: the land of
decisions.reason: The angel brings Israel to these peoples' land; Balanced and Readable say so.

source.text: לֹֽא־תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֤ה לֵאלֹֽהֵיהֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א תָֽעָבְדֵ֔ם וְלֹ֥א תַעֲשֶׂ֖ה כְּמַֽעֲשֵׂיהֶ֑ם כִּ֤י הָרֵס֙ תְּהָ֣רְסֵ֔ם וְשַׁבֵּ֥ר תְּשַׁבֵּ֖ר מַצֵּבֹתֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Not you must bow down to their gods and not you must be enticed to serve them, and not you must make like their works, for completely you will tear them down and totally you will shatter into pieces their sacred pillars.

en.L: You shall not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor do according to their works; but you shall utterly tear them down and smash their pillars to pieces.
en.B: Do not bow down to their gods or serve them, and do not copy what they do. Instead, you are to pull those gods down completely and break their sacred pillars into pieces.
en.R: Do not bow down to their gods or worship them. Do not do the things those nations do. Instead, tear down their idols completely and smash the stone pillars they worship.

decisions.choice: do according to their works: follow the peoples' religious practices
decisions.reason: Their works are what the Canaanite peoples did in worship of their gods (Leviticus 18:3).

decisions.choice: tear them down: their gods, that is, their images
decisions.reason: "Them" most naturally refers to "their gods" at the start of the verse, meaning the images and shrines that stood for those gods (34:13; Deuteronomy 7:5).

decisions.choice: pillars: standing stones set up for worship
decisions.reason: These were stones set upright as markers of a god's presence at a shrine. Israel had once set up such stones to God (Genesis 28:18; Exodus 24:4), but Canaanite pillars were to be smashed (Deuteronomy 12:3).

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: Readable says "worship" for serving other gods.

source.text: וַעֲבַדְתֶּ֗ם אֵ֚ת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם וּבֵרַ֥ךְ אֶֽת־לַחְמְךָ֖ וְאֶת־מֵימֶ֑יךָ וַהֲסִרֹתִ֥י מַחֲלָ֖ה מִקִּרְבֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will serve Yahweh your God, and he will bless your food and your water, and I will remove sickness from your midst.

en.L: And you shall serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bless your bread and your water; and I will remove sickness from your midst.
en.B: Serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bless your bread and your water. I will take sickness away from among you.
en.R: Worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bless your food and water. I will take disease away from you.

decisions.choice: he will bless ... I will remove: God speaks of himself in the third person and then the first
decisions.reason: The change of person is common in God's speeches in the law and does not mean a different speaker (compare verse 19). The ancient Greek translation reads "I will bless"; this note comes from memory and should be checked.

decisions.choice: I will remove sickness: God as Israel's healer
decisions.reason: The promise recalls 15:26, where God said he would put none of the diseases of Egypt on Israel, for "I am Yahweh your healer".

decisions.choice: Worship
decisions.reason: Readable says "worship" for serving God here.

source.text: לֹ֥א תִהְיֶ֛ה מְשַׁכֵּלָ֥ה וַעֲקָרָ֖ה בְּאַרְצֶ֑ךָ אֶת־מִסְפַּ֥ר יָמֶ֖יךָ אֲמַלֵּֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: Not anyone will be miscarrying and barren in your land; the number of your days I will complete.

en.L: There shall not be [one] miscarrying or barren in your land; the number of your days I will fill.
en.B: No woman in your land will lose her child before birth or be unable to bear children. I will let you live out the full number of your days.
en.R: No woman in your land will lose a baby before it is born, and none will be unable to have children. I will give you long, full lives.

decisions.choice: miscarrying or barren: women who lose their young or cannot bear
decisions.reason: Both words are feminine. The first is used of losing young before birth (Genesis 31:38), the second of a woman who cannot conceive (Genesis 11:30). The promise reaches to the flocks as well (Deuteronomy 7:14).

decisions.choice: I will fill the number of your days: you will live a full life
decisions.reason: God will let his people reach the full span of life, not be cut off early (Psalm 55:24; Isaiah 65:20).

source.text: אֶת־אֵֽימָתִי֙ אֲשַׁלַּ֣ח לְפָנֶ֔יךָ וְהַמֹּתִי֙ אֶת־כָּל־הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּבֹ֖א בָּהֶ֑ם וְנָתַתִּ֧י אֶת־כָּל־אֹיְבֶ֛יךָ אֵלֶ֖יךָ עֹֽרֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: My terror I will send before you, and I will confuse every people among whom you will go, and I will give all your enemies to you [as] neck.

en.L: My terror I will send before you, and I will throw into confusion all the people among whom you come, and I will make all your enemies [turn their] neck to you.
en.B: I will send terror of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ahead of you and throw every people you come against into panic. I will make all your enemies show you their backs.
en.R: I will make the nations afraid of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} before you arrive. I will cause panic among every people you go up against, and all your enemies will turn and run from you.

decisions.choice: my terror: the dread God sends on the nations
decisions.reason: It is the fear of God that seizes Israel's enemies before battle, as Moses' song foretold (15:14-16; Joshua 2:9-11).

decisions.choice: throw into confusion: put into panic
decisions.reason: The verb is used of God putting an army into panic in battle (14:24; Joshua 10:10).

decisions.choice: give your enemies to you as a neck: make them turn their backs and flee
decisions.reason: To show someone the back of the neck is to turn and run (2 Samuel 22:41; Psalm 18:41).

source.text: וְשָׁלַחְתִּ֥י אֶת־הַצִּרְעָ֖ה לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וְגֵרְשָׁ֗ה אֶת־הַחִוִּ֧י אֶת־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֛י וְאֶת־הַחִתִּ֖י מִלְּפָנֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will send the hornet before you, and it will drive out the Hivite[s], the Canaanite[s] and the Hittite[s] from before you.

en.L: And I will send the hornet before you, and it will drive out the Hivites, the Canaanites and the Hittites from before you.
en.B: I will send the hornet in front of you, and it will chase the Hivites, the Canaanites and the Hittites out of your path.
en.R: I will send hornets ahead of you. They will chase away the Hivites, the Canaanites and the Hittites as you come.

decisions.choice: the hornet: the meaning of the word is uncertain
decisions.reason: The word appears only here, in Deuteronomy 7:20 and in Joshua 24:12, each time of something God sends to drive out the peoples of Canaan. It is usually taken as "hornet", a stinging insect, either real or a picture of a terror that drives people to flight. Others understand it as "discouragement" or "panic", in line with verse 27. Joshua 24:12 says it was not by Israel's sword or bow.

decisions.choice: the Hivites, the Canaanites and the Hittites: three of the peoples of verse 23, standing for all
decisions.reason: Three names stand for the whole list.

source.text: לֹ֧א אֲגָרְשֶׁ֛נּוּ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ בְּשָׁנָ֣ה אֶחָ֑ת פֶּן־תִּהְיֶ֤ה הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ שְׁמָמָ֔ה וְרַבָּ֥ה עָלֶ֖יךָ חַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Not I will drive it out from before you in a year one, lest it should become, the land, a waste, and it will become many on you, the animal[s] of the field.

en.L: I will not drive them out from before you in one year, lest the land become a desolation and the animal[s] of the field multiply against you.
en.B: Yet I will not clear them away from before you within one year. If I did, the land would lie empty, and the wild animals would multiply and overrun you.
en.R: But I will not force them all out in one year. If I did, much of the land would be left empty, and wild animals would increase and become a danger to you.

decisions.choice: not in one year: God's care in the pace of the conquest
decisions.reason: The gradual driving out is not a failure of God's power but care for his people: an emptied land would go wild before Israel could fill it (Deuteronomy 7:22). Judges 2:20-3:4 gives a further reason why some peoples remained.

decisions.choice: the animal of the field: wild animals
decisions.reason: The phrase means wild beasts, which multiply where people are few (2 Kings 17:25-26).

source.text: מְעַ֥ט מְעַ֛ט אֲגָרְשֶׁ֖נּוּ מִפָּנֶ֑יךָ עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּפְרֶ֔ה וְנָחַלְתָּ֖ אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Little little I will drive it out from before you, until that you will be fruitful and you will possess the land.

en.L: Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you are fruitful and possess the land.
en.B: I will drive them out from before you little by little, until you have grown many and can take the land as your own.
en.R: I will push them out a little at a time, until there are enough of you to take over the whole land.

decisions.choice: little by little: a little at a time
decisions.reason: The word "little" is doubled to mean bit by bit, a stage at a time (Deuteronomy 7:22).

decisions.choice: be fruitful and possess: grow in number and take the land as an inheritance
decisions.reason: "Be fruitful" echoes the blessing of Genesis 1:28 and the growth of Israel in Egypt (1:7). The second verb means to receive as an inheritance.

source.text: וְשַׁתִּ֣י אֶת־גְּבֻלְךָ֗ מִיַּם־סוּף֙ וְעַד־יָ֣ם פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וּמִמִּדְבָּ֖ר עַד־הַנָּהָ֑ר כִּ֣י׀אֶתֵּ֣ן בְּיֶדְכֶ֗ם אֵ֚ת יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ וְגֵרַשְׁתָּ֖מוֹ מִפָּנֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will set your border from [the] sea of reed[s] and to the sea of [the] Philistines, and from [the] wilderness to the River; for I will give into your hand the inhabitants of the land, and you will drive them out from before you.

en.L: And I will set your border from the Sea of Reeds to the sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River; for I will give into your hand the inhabitants of the land, and you shall drive them out from before you.
en.B: I will fix your borders from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the Euphrates River. I will hand over to you the people who live in the land, and you will drive them out before you.
en.R: Your land will stretch from the Red Sea to the Mediterranean Sea, and from the desert to the Euphrates River. I will put the people who live there in your power, and you will force them out as you advance.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Reeds: here the gulf on the southeast of the land
decisions.reason: See the note at 10:19 on the name. Here, at the southern edge of the promised land, it most likely means the gulf east of Sinai, on whose shore Ezion-geber stood (1 Kings 9:26).

decisions.choice: the sea of the Philistines ... the wilderness ... the River: the Mediterranean, the southern desert and the Euphrates
decisions.reason: The sea of the Philistines is the Mediterranean, on whose coast the Philistines lived. The wilderness is the desert to the south, and "the River" here is the Euphrates, as in the promise to Abraham (Genesis 15:18; Deuteronomy 11:24; 1 Kings 5:1).

decisions.choice: the Euphrates River
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in Exodus "the River" is the Nile; here it is the Euphrates, so Balanced and Readable name it. Readable also names the Mediterranean for "the sea of the Philistines". Literal keeps "the River".

source.text: לֹֽא־תִכְרֹ֥ת לָהֶ֛ם וְלֵאלֹֽהֵיהֶ֖ם בְּרִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: Not you must make with them and with their gods a covenant.

en.L: You shall not make with them or with their gods a covenant.
en.B: Make no covenant with them or with their gods.
en.R: Do not make any agreement with those peoples or with their gods.

decisions.choice: no covenant with them or their gods: Israel belongs to one covenant only
decisions.reason: A treaty with the peoples of Canaan would bind Israel to their gods as well, since such treaties were sworn by the gods of both sides. Israel is bound to Yahweh alone (34:12, 15; Deuteronomy 7:2; Joshua 9).

decisions.choice: agreement
decisions.reason: Readable says "agreement" for a covenant between peoples.

source.text: לֹ֤א יֵשְׁבוּ֙ בְּאַרְצְךָ֔ פֶּן־יַחֲטִ֥יאוּ אֹתְךָ֖ לִ֑י כִּ֤י תַעֲבֹד֙ אֶת־אֱלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ם כִּֽי־יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֖ לְמוֹקֵֽשׁ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Not they will dwell in your land, lest they cause you to sin against me, for you will serve their gods, for it will become for you a snare.

en.L: They shall not dwell in your land, lest they make you sin against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; for you will serve their gods, for it will be a snare to you."
en.B: They must not live in your land, or they will lead you to sin against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. For you would come to serve their gods, and that would be a snare to you."
en.R: Do not let them stay in your land. They would lead you to sin against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You would begin to worship their gods, and that would catch you like a trap."

decisions.choice: for you will serve their gods, for it will be a snare: the danger explained
alternatives: if you serve their gods, it will surely be a snare to you
decisions.reason: The two clauses may be read as cause and result ("for you would serve their gods, and that would be a snare") or as a condition ("if you serve their gods, it will surely be a snare"). Either way the presence of these peoples leads to their worship, and their worship to ruin (34:12; Judges 2:3).

decisions.choice: a snare: a trap that catches its prey
decisions.reason: The word is a hunter's trap. The worship of other gods would catch Israel and bring it down (Deuteronomy 7:16; Psalm 106:36).

decisions.choice: the end of God's words
decisions.reason: The speech that began at 20:22 ends here; in 24:1 the narrative takes up again.

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: Readable says "worship" for serving other gods.
